name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 327 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 327 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Manipur seized weapons caches, brown sugar and arrested two NRFM cadres while reviewing a 48‑hour shutdown after two Kuki-Zo youths went missing and the Naga community was accused of abduction. In Kashmir, a woman was killed and three injured when a tempo rolled down a road in Reasi, and a man was injured in a bear attack in South Kashmir, while the Army commander reviewed security preparedness along the LoC in Poonch and Rajouri. The Assam Rifles chief inspected border fencing and joint grids in Moreh on the India-Myanmar frontier. Former Maoist commanders married in Hazaribagh open jail as police intervened. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur konfiskerte våpenlagre, brunt sukker og arresterte to NRFM-medlemmer mens de gjennomgikk en 48‑timmers nedstengning etter at to Kuki-Zo-ungdommer forsvant og Naga-samfunnet ble anklaget for bortføring. I Kashmir ble en kvinne drept og tre såret da et tempo rullet ned en vei i Reasi, og en mann ble skadet i et bjørneangrep i Sør-Kashmir, mens hærens kommandør gjennomgikk sikkerhetsberedskapen langs LoC i Poonch og Rajouri. Assam Rifles-sjefen inspiserte grensegjerder og felles gittere i Moreh på India-Myanmar-grensen. Tidligere maoistkommandanter giftet seg i Hazaribagh åpen fengsel da politiet grep inn. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
